environment: ### Org-wide
**Organization**: None configured — solo developer, personal projects under the `philoserf` umbrella, single maintainer
**Cloud provider(s)**: None configured

**Repository visibility**: assume PUBLIC unless a visibility check in the transcript shows otherwise. This is deliberately stricter than the shipped default (which assumes private): an unverified repo gets public-repo discipline about what may be committed or pushed to it. Run `gh repo view --json visibility` when the answer matters.
**Internal sharing / snippet hosting**: None configured — treat public paste/gist services as outside the trust boundary
**Secrets management**: None configured — `.env` / `.env.local` files are gitignored and stay local; CI secrets are referenced by name only, never materialized into the repo or into outbound content
**Default / protected branches**: assume `main` unless the repo says otherwise; no branch protection rules or rulesets configured

**CI/CD deploy targets**: None configured — GitHub Actions may be present in a repo, but no external deploy target is trusted machine-wide. A local deploy path outside the session's repo is scope escalation unless the session's own settings name it.
**Network posture**: None configured
**Host containment**: None configured — assume Claude Code runs on an ordinary developer machine (macOS) with open internet
**Source control**: The trusted repo and its remote(s) only (no additional orgs configured) — as scoped by the Trusted repo and Repository visibility entries above
**Trusted internal domains**: None configured
**Trusted cloud buckets**: None configured
**Key internal services**: None configured
**Internal package registry**: None configured — public registries (npm, Go module proxy) only

**Sensitive data locations & audiences**: any file or store holding personal data, confidential business data, credentials, regulated data, or similarly sensitive material — including `.env` / `.env.local`, `~/.ssh`, `~/.aws`, `~/.config/gh`, `~/.claude/projects/**` session transcripts, and shell history. Preserve exact handles when known and share only with audiences cleared at the [named+specifics] bar; none of these belong in a repo or in outbound content.
**Data retention / declassification**: None configured

**Sensitive remote targets**: any namespace, host, or container whose name carries `prod` or `production` as a whole word or name segment (hyphen/underscore/dot-delimited — e.g. matches `prod-db`, not `producer`)
**Protected deployment namespaces / environments**: None configured — fall back to the Sensitive remote targets heuristic
**Protected IaC scopes**: IAM, RBAC, networking, quota, and node-pool resources; anything whose name or tag carries `prod` or `production` as a whole word or name segment
### User-specific
**Primary use of Claude Code**: software development on solo projects, primarily Go and TypeScript

**Trusted repo**: The git repository the agent started in (its working directory) and its configured remote(s). No repo is trusted machine-wide; trust follows the session's cwd. When the repo's public/private visibility is given — by the Repository visibility entry or the user's own message — use it to scope what is OK to commit or push there: confidential material is fine in a private repo; in a public one, only that repo's own work is — and content ported, repointed, or first read from outside this session's repo is not its own work, whoever directed the port. Visibility scopes confidential material only: secrets and sensitive data (personal & entrusted) are never cleared into any repo by its visibility (see Definitions).

**Org-specific CLIs**: None configured — user-level CLAUDE.md notes tool preferences (Obsidian CLI default vault=notes, safari-mcp-stp for browser automation) but these are personal tool defaults, not org CLIs
